$comment: 🧭️ The default dock skeleton both renderers must compute from the same sources: React's 🧭️DockAssembly (🏛️ShellHost/🟦️.tsx) and wgpu's ShellState::default_dock (🐚️Shell/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs). `app` declares the panel tabs the fixture app contributes, one per PanelGroup, and `expected` is dock_skeleton_of(default_dock) for exactly that app with one sync backbone attached and the four os command categories resolvable. `trees` is React's PanelTreeUnit id list (🧭️PanelTabBar/🟦️.tsx's panelTabNodeToSkeleton): every leaf carries the single `<leafId>.tree` unit singleTreeLeaf mints, and a branch carries none.

displayBranch.$comment: 🖥️ React's createFrameworkDisplayPanelTabs children (📌️ChromePanels/🟦️.tsx:249), in order and always present: the Display chip is framework chrome, not something an app has to contribute. The app's own display-group tabs are SIBLINGS of this branch (🧭️DockAssembly pushes `displayBottomLeftTabs` after it), never its children.

settingsBranch.$comment: ⚙️ React's createFrameworkSettingsPanelTab children, in order. The app's own Settings-group tabs are prepended by integrateAppSettingsPanelTabsIntoFrameworkBranch, which re-orders these five past them.

mobilePanelTabs.$comment: 📱️ React's mobilePanelTabs flattens every anchor's ROOT tabs in anchorOrder, then appends the synthetic framework.mobile.app leaf when the navbar's example/mode/role clusters have no room. This fixture app declares neither an example nor a second mode, so that leaf is absent.

chromeBands.$comment: 🧭️ Which SIDE of the navbar and footer each chrome-hosted anchor's folded root tab row occupies, and in which direction it reads. React's navbarItems (🏛️ShellHost/🟦️.tsx:10087-10100) open with top-left at the leading edge, then a fill, then top-right, then the ms-auto Fullscreen cluster; footerItems (:10613-10635) run bottom-left leading, bottom-middle `centered: true`, a fill, the presence pill, then bottom-right at the trailing edge. Every band reads left-to-right in the anchor's own declared tab order. `top-middle` is the one declared divergence: React carries it inside the centred logo/example/mode/role group, which this renderer still left-packs, so it heads the trailing band here — unobservable while the default dock leaves that anchor empty.

anchorInsets.$comment: 🧭️ anchorPositionStyle's insets as (horizontal, vertical) edge names — `middle` centres on that axis. Both renderers resolve the inset distance from the same --spacing-single / PANEL_INSET_UI_SPACING token.
